articles.title: Real Sociedad ease Hearts out of Europa Cup
articles.summary: Heart of Midlothian exit the Women's Europa Cup after Real Sociedad sweep to a convincing 4-0 victory in the second leg of their second qualifying round tie.
articles.body:
Heart of Midlothian exited the Women's Europa Cup after Real Sociedad swept to a convincing 4-0 victory in the second leg of their second qualifying round tie.

With the sides having finished goalless last week in Edinburgh, the Scottish champions rarely threatened to break their duck in San Sebastian.

Real had all the pressure and it told after 18 minutes as winger Laura Camino superbly headed Ainhoa Marin's cross inside the far post from 12 yards.

Hearts' hopes of reaching the break level ended five minutes from half time when Erin Rennie pulled down rival midfielder Intza Egiguren and Paula Fernandez slotted the spot kick.

The hosts added to that four minutes later when Cecilia Marcos' low cross was prodded home from close range by fellow midfielder Ainoa Campo.

Torrential rain stemmed the home flow as Lauren Wade fired Hearts' first effort on goal straight at the home goalkeeper from a 55th-minute free-kick.

However, Marin prodded in the hosts' fourth after 76 minutes.

articles.title: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald shares heartfelt message about Chargers' Jim Harbaugh
articles.summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald had nothing but praise for Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh ahead of their Week 4 matchup.
articles.body:
The Chargers are looking for their first win of the season in Week 4, but it won't be easy as they face the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks .

It'll be a tall task, as the Chargers will head to the Pacific Northwest for their second road game of the season.

Seattle's crowd is rowdy, and head coach Mike Macdonald has led the team back to where they were in the early to mid 2010s. Macdonald was clearly a home run hire for the Seahawks; however, before that, he was one of Jim Harbaugh's coordinators.

The two spent the 2021 season together in Michigan, and Macdonald will never forget it. Before their Week 4 matchup, Macdonald reevaluated why he's forever grateful to the Harbaugh family, especially Jim.

"I had the honor of working for both Jim and John, one year with Jim," Macdonald said .

"He [Jim] gave me so much autonomy and, like, the belief that he had in our staff on defense and in me personally as well.

"It felt like he never left your corner. We had a blast that year in Ann Arbor, and I'm just proud to say that we worked for him and are proud of the year that we had."

Harbaugh and Macdonald spent the 2021 season together at Michigan. Macdonald served as the Wolverines' defensive coordinator, leading them to a top-10 national defense, an undefeated home record, the Big Ten Conference Championship, and a College Football Playoff appearance.

The Wolverines finished No. 3 overall that season and went 12-2.

After that lone season, Macdonald spent two seasons as the Ravens ' defensive coordinator before the Seahawks hired him as head coach.

articles.title: England: Impossible for Three Lions to find another Harry Kane - Thomas Tuchel
articles.summary: England boss Thomas Tuchel says it will be impossible to find "another Harry Kane" as his free-scoring captain continues to break new ground.
articles.body:
England boss Thomas Tuchel says it will be impossible to find "another Harry Kane" as his free-scoring captain continues to break new ground.

Kane scored a record-extending 87th goal for the Three Lions against the Czech Republic on Tuesday.

And he is now just two appearances away from equalling Peter Shilton's mark of 125 international appearances as he hones in on becoming England's most capped player ever.

However, while the 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward is in the form of his life, with his 73 goals for club and country last term putting him well into the conversation as a possible Ballon d'Or winner, he cannot go on forever and Tuchel admitted that there is no obvious successor.

"You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all," Tuchel said.

"He is the first one to push everyone and that is his mindset and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills. He is a complete package.

"We look for different options and solutions. We finished the game with Jude [Bellingham] up front as a number nine.

"There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years."

Kane is one of the leading strikers of his generation, but finding a suitable back-up has been a long-standing problem for England.

Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney utilised that role at the past two major tournaments but the Saudi Arabia-based pair are also in their thirties and were overlooked for the current batch of Nations League fixtures.

While Dominic Calvert-Lewin is in the squad, he is also approaching his 30th birthday and Liam Delap is currently the only English centre forward under the age of 27 to have scored a Champions League goal.

And that means Tuchel supplemented his striking options in Prague by deploying Real Madrid star Bellingham in a more advanced role than his normal midfield position after bringing him on for Kane.

"I like him as a nine," Tuchel added. "Then he can contribute to both sides and overload the sides and doesn't affect so much of the balance.

"We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides. We are working on that.

"He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to be there and have the decisive action, so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a nine or a 10."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves Portugal's camp due to reported rift with manager
articles.summary: Ronaldo did not appear during Sunday's win over Norway and was not set to start against Denmark on Thursday.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal 's national team camp one day before its UEFA Nations League game against Denmark .

In an Instagram post, Ronaldo announced he was leaving the team after manager Jorge Jesus said he was planning to not start the 41-year-old.

"Following the press conference with the National Team Coach, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have made the decision to leave the National Team training camp," Ronaldo wrote. "In due course, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that motivated my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated. "Now it is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception."

"Following the press conference with the National Team Coach, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have made the decision to leave the National Team training camp," Ronaldo wrote.

"In due course, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that motivated my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

"Now it is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception."

Ronaldo did not play during Sunday's 2-1 win over Norway . Jesus said that he told the five-time Ballon d'Or winner he would likely be a part of the match, but changed course based on how the game was going.

Jesus acknowledged he was wrong to have Ronaldo warm up and not use him, but he did not apologize for telling the player he would likely be involved.

"I can promise whatever I want, I'm the coach," said Jesus, who replaced Roberto Martínez four days after Portugal was eliminated by eventual World Cup champion Spain in the Round of 16. "No player will ever make a decision for me."

Jesus, who coached Ronaldo last season in Saudi Arabia with Al-Nassr, said in a pregame news conference before Ronaldo departed camp that the players understand the manager makes the decisions and that Ronaldo told him he was fine with that.

"It seems like there was an issue between us, but there was no issue," Jesus said. "I'm the one who makes the decisions and everybody knows that."

The situation led to a meeting with Jesus, Pedro Proença, president of the Portugese Football Federation, and Ronaldo, but Jesus said "there was nothing to solve."

Ronaldo's only appearance for Portugal during this international window came last Thursday during a 1-0 win over Wales. He played 67 minutes before being substituted.

articles.title: Lamine se divierte
articles.standfirst: El extremo mostró su mejor versión ante Inglaterra y Croacia.
articles.summary: El extremo mostró su mejor versión ante Inglaterra y Croacia.
articles.body: Como dirían los chicos de su edad, Lamine Yamal está en su 'prime'. Es decir, en su mejor versión. La más disfrutona, la más feliz, la más alegre y la más desequilibrante. Lo demuestra dentro del campo y lo admite fuera de él. "Ya dije antes del partido contra el Feyenoord que es el momento en el que más feliz estoy. Estoy disfrutando mucho", aseguró tras marcar dos goles y asistir ante Croacia. Y es precisamente esa versión alegre de Lamine la que lo catapulta en pleno debate sobre el Balón de Oro. La votación ya está cerrada y lo que ha pasado en el arranque de esta nueva temporada no computaba, pero probablemente sí influye. "No sólo juego para este Balón de Oro. Juego para mí, para la afición y para seguir ganando. No sólo jugamos sólo por eso", admite. Durante el Mundial muchos echaron de menos al Lamine más influyente de cara al gol. Sólo anotó en la goleada frente a Arabia Saudí y casi no sale en ninguna fotografía de momentos determinantes donde los focos apuntaron a Ferran, Oyarzabal o Merino, pero él siempre aportó lo suyo. Arrastraba rivales para generar espacios, intentaba desbordar y su presencia siempre era un quebradero de cabeza para el rival. Todo ello no era suficiente para los críticos. Y tampoco para él: "Después de ganar el Mundial no estaba contento. Hice muchas cosas que la gente no vio. Para un entrenador es increíble tener a un jugador que arrastra a tres rivales, pero yo no estaba contento por mí. Otro jugador con mi rendimiento hubiera hecho un gran Mundial, pero yo creo que podría haber hecho más", confesaba en Universo Valdano. Esa versión óptima de Lamine es la que estamos disfrutando en esta ventana de partidos internacionales. En Wembley, frente a Inglaterra, jugó uno de sus mejores partidos con la camiseta de la selección. Marcó el primer gol del partido, estuvo desatado en el uno contra uno y repartió caramelos a Olmo y Ferran que se quedaron cerca de convertir en gol. Además, fue solidario en defensa, recuperó balones en campo contrario y supo ralentizar el juego cuando tocó. En Sevilla fue capaz de mejorar la versión que vimos en Londres. Marcó dos goles y asistió a Pubill en otro. Más allá de los números, volvió a ser dominador e indomable. "Hace un mes decíais que estaba mal, que no sabíais qué me pasaba. Yo estoy tranquilo, sigo disfrutando. Sé que en cualquier momento vais a volver a decir lo mismo, así que estoy tranquilo", reclamaba ante los medios. Lamine ha empezado la temporada en plena forma en el Barça y en la selección. En los últimos 8 partidos acumula 11 goles y 7 asistencias. Una influencia directa en 18 de los últimos 36 goles que ha logrado en su club y en la selección. "Es un jugador especial. Es jugador increíble y lo estáis viendo todos. Espero que siga así, trabajando con la humildad que él tiene. El que sepa de fútbol y le guste disfrutar del fútbol sabe que es el mejor", confesó Nico Williams.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president has 'no place in future of football', says computer hacker Rui Pinto
articles.summary: The computer hacker who released documents which led to the Premier League investigation into Manchester City says Gianni Infantino "should have no place in the future of the game".
articles.body:
The computer hacker who released documents which led to the Premier League investigation into Manchester City says Fifa president Gianni Infantino "should have no place in the future of the game".

City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, though they continue to deny any wrongdoing and have until 2 October to submit an appeal.

The Premier League investigation was launched following information released into the public domain by the Football Leaks website in 2018, via German publication Der Spiegel, and following a separate investigation by European football's governing body Uefa.

In a message on X , external , Rui Pinto, creator of Football Leaks, repeated allegations from 2018 that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football's governing body Uefa.

According to a report by Der Spiegel , external , the clubs overvalued sponsorship deals to help meet FFP rules and, when facing sanctions over the matter, the allegations in the documents state Infantino helped arrange more lenient punishments for them in 2014.

A PSG statement at the time said it "has always acted in full compliance with the laws and regulations enacted by sports institutions" and it "denies the allegations".

"Since the introduction of Financial Fair Play, Paris St-Germain have been one of the most audited and scrutinised clubs in history," the club added.

"Back in 2014, there was a man who was already aware of the irregularities involving Manchester City," 37-year-old Portuguese Pinto wrote on Wednesday.

"The infamous Gianni Infantino, then Uefa general secretary, abused his authority, shared confidential documents and, in short, outmanoeuvred the investigatory chamber, doing everything in his power to ensure that both Manchester City and PSG would merely receive a fine, avoiding a deeper investigation that could have led to a Champions League ban.

"All of these details were also revealed through Football Leaks.

"Given his actions as Uefa general secretary and, more recently, as Fifa president, I can only say, in my humble opinion, that Gianni Infantino has become a cancer on football and should have no place in the future of the game."

When the allegations first surfaced, Uefa stressed that it was within the remit of the general secretary to assist in such matters, adding: "This may include discussions, meetings, assistance to help find solutions, and other interactions to assist the [investigating body] in its work."

Infantino similarly pointed to how his "job entails having discussions, having conversations, exchanging documents, drafts, ideas, whatever, on many, many, many, many, topics.

"So if then this is being portrayed as something bad, I think there's not much I can do more than my job in an honest way, in a professional way and trying to defend the interests of football."

BBC Sport has contacted Fifa following Pinto's latest statement.

Infantino has come under increasing pressure following his now-shelved plans to sell stakes in the World Cup.

European football's governing body Uefa accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, while the Swiss Football Association (SFV) is the latest association to withdraw its support for the Fifa president.

"The decision follows a comprehensive reassessment of developments over the past few months," an SFV statement read.

"From the SFV's perspective, various incidents raise fundamental questions regarding leadership, governance, transparency and decision-making processes within Fifa."

Both Fifa and Uefa are based in Switzerland.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

articles.title: Europa Cup: Rangers' hopes ended by classy Hammarby
articles.summary: Rangers exit the Europa Cup after last season's finalists Hammarby leave Broadwood Stadium with a three-goal victory on the night to progress 5-0 on aggregate.
articles.body:
Rangers exited the Europa Cup after last season's finalists Hammarby left Broadwood Stadium with a three-goal victory on the night to progress 5-0 on aggregate.

It took only 13 minutes for the side sitting second in the 2026 Swedish top flight to add to their first-leg lead.

Defender Mathilde Janzen found Anna Walter with a fine through ball and the midfielder slotted it wide of exposed goalkeeper Jenna Fife.

Rangers' first threat came after 21 minutes, with striker Laura Berry firing straight at goalkeeper Cajsa Andersson.

However, Hammarby should have extended their lead before the break, with Iceland striker Ida Hermannsdottir and midfielder Elin Sorum squandering chances from close range.

For all the Scottish Women's Premier League leaders' possession, it took until the 58th minute to threaten again, with Berry firing straight at Andersson.

Two minutes later, the tie was over as Hermannsdottir strode gracefully into the path of a superb through ball before another clinical finish for last season's Swedish league runners-up.

An emphatic victory was secured as 16-year-old midfielder Fanny Peterson added to her first-leg goal as she pounced after Svea Rehnberg's close-range effort was parried by Fife.

That ended Scotland's hopes in the Europe's second-tier competition after champions Heart of Midlothian's defeat earlier in the evening by Real Sociedad.

articles.title: Cristiano y Messi: Maneras de vivir
articles.standfirst: Ambos afrontan su adiós definitivo a la selección como dos polos opuestos
articles.summary: Ambos afrontan su adiós definitivo a la selección como dos polos opuestos
articles.body: Siempre fueron como agua y aceite. Los dos mejores, tan extraordinarios, tan distintos. Messi transcurría su carrera sin levantar la voz y encogido ante los micrófonos. Cristiano sonreía y posaba para los focos mientras proclamaba sus virtudes a los cuatro vientos. Los dos dominaban el fútbol, pero de manera bien distinta. Hoy, Cristiano se va de su selección por la puerta de atrás, dando un portazo, con una rabieta de adolescente. A miles de kilómetros, Argentina prepara toda una ceremonia para el adiós programado, y medido al milímetro, de su leyenda. Es el vivo ejemplo de lo que son dos personalidades completamente distintas. Y eso que Messi amagó con una prematura despedida de la albiceleste, pero siempre con tacto, con los pasos medidos y cargado de argumentos. Quiso echarse a un lado para que Argentina pudiese avanzar. Cristiano nunca ha dudado de su idoneidad en un puesto que, en los últimos tiempos, se le ha quedado grande. Y ahora se va enfrentado con el seleccionador, en medio de una crisis interna, a la carrera hacia el aeropuerto para poner pies en polvorosa a bordo de su avión privado. Todo demasiado artificial. Es algo que se ha repetido hasta la saciedad en el mundo del deporte: hay que saber retirarse a tiempo. Cristiano, animal competitivo donde los haya, no ha aceptado un papel secundario. Ni siquiera sus discretas actuaciones en las dos grandes citas de Portugal -ningún gol en la Eurocopa y dos goles ante Uzbekistán en el Mundial- le han aplicado una dosis de realismo a la leyenda lusa. Las comparaciones, ya saben, son odiosas. Y mientras CR7 no ha sabido medir los tiempos y ceder protagonismo, su eterno rival rozó la gloria en Estados Unidos después de un Mundial inolvidable y, acto seguido, entendió que retirarse en lo más alto es lo lógico y lo oportuno para alguien de su condición. Cristiano está a tiempo de rectificar. Él y Portugal se merecen otro final. Pero el orgullo es un difícil acompañante a la hora de abrazar la concordia. Nunca fue algo que le acompañase en su carrera. Y tampoco iba a ser ahora una excepción. Un adiós inesperado, triste, pero, al fin y al cabo, al más puro estilo Cristiano.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain leaves squad amid reported rift with head coach Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Portugal's captain announces he has walked out of the camp "following the national team manager's press conference" in a post on Instagram after reports of a rift between the pair; Portugal boss Jorge Jesus denied there was an incident after he left Ronaldo on the bench vs Norway
articles.body:
Reports of a rift between Ronaldo and Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus emerged after the six-time Ballon d'Or winner was left as an unused substitute in Sunday's Nations League win over Norway.

Jesus, who was Ronaldo's coach at Al Nassr, insisted "there was no incident whatsoever" in his press conference on Wednesday, claiming the star was set to return to training with his team-mates ahead of Thursday's Nations League game against Denmark in Copenhagen.

However, Ronaldo announced he had walked out on Portugal's camp later on Wednesday in a cryptic post on Instagram.

The 41-year-old wrote: "Following the national team manager's press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I decided to leave the national team's training camp.

"In due course, I will tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

"Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception."

Spanish ​outlet Marca reported earlier on Wednesday that Ronaldo, who is Portugal's record goalscorer and most-capped player of all time, took a private ‌jet to Madrid.

Ronaldo has not participated in Portugal training since Sunday's Norway win, which saw his replacement, Goncalo Ramos, score.

The Al Nassr forward started in Portugal's Nations League-opening home win over Wales last Thursday on a frustrating night for Ronaldo.

He missed a slew of chances and had a second-half effort ruled out by a VAR intervention before being taken off in the 67th minute.

His appearance against Wales was cap number 234 for Portugal, but his decision to leave the camp ahead of Thursday's Denmark game raises huge doubts over whether he will add to that tally in the future.

Ronaldo admitted during this camp with Portugal that he considered international retirement after his disappointing World Cup performance drew widespread criticism.

Across a 23-year international career, Ronaldo has scored 146 times in 234 appearances for Portugal. He has made no secret of wanting to reach 1,000 career goals - his current tally is 979 - but may have to achieve that feat in club football.

Analysis: Ronaldo's latest move leaves 'bad taste'

Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"Another day, another big Cristiano Ronaldo story. He is a man who has been making headlines for 23 years with Portugal. This latest story, though, leaves a bit of a bad taste in the mouth.

"Ronaldo was a substitue in Portugal's game against Norway on Sunday night, which they won 2-1, and he was expecting to come on as a substitute.

"But the Portugal manager Jorge Jesus decided not to use him. He said, 'I planned to use him, but the circumstances weren't right for him to be introduced during that game'.

"Ronaldo appears not to have taken this snub very well because he has not trained with his teammates since that game, he had been training in the gym, and he has now confirmed he has left the camp."

articles.title: Louzán: "Vamos a organizar la final del Mundial en España"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la RFEF atendió a los medios en el descanso del España-México Sub 20
articles.summary: El presidente de la RFEF atendió a los medios en el descanso del España-México Sub 20
articles.body: Rafael Louzán atendió a los medios en el intermedio del amistoso entre las selecciones Sub 20 de España y México celebrado en el Cerro del Espino para dibujar el mejor de los panoramas posibles para el fútbol español. El presidente de la Federación habló de "momento de oro", esquivó la polémica arbitral que persigue al fútbol nacional y reservó su mensaje más rotundo para la gran final del Mundial 2030, que reclama para suelo español sin fisuras. Sobre el jugador que donará su prima a los trabajadores de la Federación: "Es un tema de organización interna y, por lo tanto, queremos solo palabras de agradecimiento. Eso es para que podamos entender todos cuáles son los valores de nuestra selección, de nuestros jugadores". Sobre el caso del Manchester City y su paralelismo con el Negreira: "No hay que especular; de momento, cuando haya sentencia sobre el caso Manchester City, hablaremos. Se nos queda un poco lejos, yo bastante tengo con lo de aquí". Sobre la supuesta inacción en España con el caso Negreira: "Estamos viviendo el momento de oro del fútbol español, yo diría de una salud extraordinaria. Hay que mirar siempre los errores y no volver a caer en ellos, pero estamos en el año dorado, aprovechémoslo". Sobre recuperar un amistoso ante México, ausente desde 2010: "¿Por qué no jugar en México? Nos han trasladado alguna posibilidad, pero el calendario da para lo que da. En el 27 muy difícil; habrá alguna opción probablemente más en el 28". Sobre la sede de la final del Mundial 2030: "El Mundial 2030 comienza en España, con España y Portugal. Es el año del centenario. Debe rematar en España y estamos trabajando para ello". Sobre las palabras de Tebas y la final condicionada a Infantino: "Para mí no existen dudas; España tiene que organizar sí o sí esa gran final y vamos a trabajar en esa línea". Sobre si es relevante que Infantino siga en la FIFA: "Eso lo tienen que decidir los 211 países que tienen derecho a voto. Primero hay que ver quién se presenta el día 18 de noviembre. Vamos a organizar la final en España".

articles.title: Las razones del enfado de Cristiano con Jorge Jesus: ¿será su despedida de Portugal?
articles.standfirst: MARCA les descubre el minuto a minuto del desencuentro entre jugador y entrenador
articles.summary: MARCA les descubre el minuto a minuto del desencuentro entre jugador y entrenador
articles.body: Cristiano no era uno más y se está comprobando. Jorge Jesus, pese a todo y todos los rumores que había, decidió convocarle para estos cuatro partidos. Pero, ¿qué ha hecho enfadar a Cristiano? ¿Cómo ha sido la cronología de los hechos? ¿Pueden ser las últimas horas de Cris con su país? 1. Jorge Jesus convoca a Cristiano y pactan que el 7 jugaría el primer partido (Gales, 1-0) y el cuarto (ante Noruega el 4 de octubre). Hasta ahí, todo bien, y Cris jugó de titular ante Gales, actuando los primeros 66 minutos, marcando un gol... pero fue anulado. Hasta ahí, todo bien. 2. En la mañana del segundo partido ante Noruega (1-2), Jorge Jesus cambia de opinión y le dice a Cristiano que lo necesita para ese choque y que quizá le da la última media hora del partido. ¿Qué pasa? El choque iba 1-1 en el 51' con gol de Haaland. Cris se pone a calentar, Portugal se pone 1-2 en el 54' y la situación del partido no da ya para que el 7 juegue pues hay que aguantar el resultado. Calienta media hora, no sale y se va enojado del estadio. 3. No entrena en la previa y se va al hotel. Cristiano, ayer martes, no entrenó con el grupo en Dinamarca y se va al hotel mientras el entreno se produce. Se entrena en solitario en el gimnasio. 4. La rueda de Prensa de JJ hace estallar a Cris. El crack escucha la rueda de Prensa de su entrenador, no le convencen sus explicaciones -"es un momento de frustración que dura 10, 15 o 20 segundos", dijo JJ- y, lejos de entrenar con el grupo, se larga de la concentración. Cogerá su avión privado rumbo a Madrid, y llegará esta noche. 5. ¿Será su despedida de la Selección? Difícil saberlo ahora, pues la cosa es muy reciente. Pero los 146 goles en 234 partidos del 7 podrían haber llegado a su fin en Portugal.

articles.title: Man City charges: Club sponsor Etihad Airways considering legal action against Premier League
articles.summary: Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023
articles.body:
City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

And now the Abu Dhabi state airline Etihad Airways, which has sponsored City since 2009, says it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".

In a statement, they say the Premier League did not engage with them and they were not given a chance to provide relevant information.

They are now seeking legal advice to protect their interests.

Etihad were not named in Tuesday's published judgment but say it has "created damaging implications" for them.

Sky Sports News has contacted the Premier League for comment.

Meanwhile, several Man City sponsors are standing by the club in the wake of the guilty verdict.

Lucozade, Kellogg's and Revolut have all told Sky Sports News they are not commenting on the independent commission's findings while the process remains ongoing.

Majestic Wines have refused to comment on whether they will continue their commercial partnership with Manchester City.

Sky Sports News is still awaiting responses from Sure, Durex, EA Sports, CP Company, Britvic, SilentNight, OKX, Gaucho and Champneys.

A statement said: "Etihad Airways has reviewed the Premier League commission's published opinion relating to the disciplinary proceedings involving Manchester City, together with the Premier League's public communication of its findings.

"Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.

"The Premier League's public communication of the commission's findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

"At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the commission's opinion. Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.

"Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.

"Etihad is immensely proud of its longstanding relationship with Manchester City. The Etihad name has been proudly carried by the club and its stadium for many years, as part of a partnership that has connected us with millions of supporters around the world. Our commitment to Manchester City, its supporters and our shared partnership remains strong.

"We stand with the club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the commission's conclusions through the processes available to it.

"Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests."

The Etihad statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission .

'Etihad statement shows how Man City will fight back'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"In 2011, Etihad Airways signed a 10-year deal which was worth £400 million, which they have since extended.

"They have released a very strongly worded statement, and in it they say they are seeking legal advice to protect their interests.

"Now, why would they be doing that? The reason behind it is that the judgment from the independent commission on Tuesday said that Manchester City's owners had been inflating their sponsorship income, and that some of City's sponsorship deals were 'sham' deals that weren't real contracts.

"They acknowledged that they weren't named in the published decision, but they say it has 'created damaging implications for Etihad Airways'.

"This just proves that Manchester City are not going to take this lying down. They are absolutely convinced that they have done nothing wrong.

"They don't believe that this has been a fair and impartial process, and we've got the situation now where their principal sponsor has come out and threatened the Premier League with legal action and said that what the commission have done and the published decision yesterday has very damaging implications for them.

"Etihad Airways are a big airline and a big business. They're one of the biggest airlines in the world, worth around £4 billion

"I think this is a very big development as it gives you a sense of how City are going to be fighting back."

What did the independent commission find?

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven.

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

A Manchester City statement released on Tuesday read: "Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission .

articles.title: Thiago Pitarch y Morante ponen la rúbrica al homenaje a Ceuta
articles.standfirst: La Sub-20 de Paco Gallardo, con el bloque campeón de Europa, venció 2-0 a México en el Cerro del Espino, con goles de Thiago Pitarch y Morante, en el partido homenaje a Ceuta trasladado desde la ciudad autónoma
articles.summary: La Sub-20 de Paco Gallardo, con el bloque campeón de Europa, venció 2-0 a México en el Cerro del Espino, con goles de Thiago Pitarch y Morante, en el partido homenaje a Ceuta trasladado desde la ciudad autónoma
articles.body: Paco Gallardo puso prácticamente toda la carne en el asador, con un once cuajado de campeones de Europa Sub-19 este pasado verano. La apuesta por sus hombres de confianza dejó claro que, pese al carácter amistoso, la Rojita salió a refrendar su condición de referencia continental. El primer aviso español llegó pronto, en un centro de Fortea que Joselillo Gaitán cabeceó con peligro y obligó a volar a Olivera. Un anticipo de lo que se cocía, porque a la siguiente España ya no perdonó. Thiago Pitarch armó con zurda un disparo desde fuera del área que se coló raso, pegadito a la cepa del palo izquierdo, sin que el meta pudiera hacer nada. Y la celebración tuvo destinatario: el propio Pitarch corrió hacia la banda para fundirse en un sentido abrazo con Paco Gallardo, gesto que retrató la comunión entre el grupo y su técnico. España, crecida, mereció ampliar la renta. Minutos después, Hugo López perdonó el segundo a pase de Salinas, y poco más tarde protagonizó una galopada que coronó con una delicatessen de tacón para que Joselillo rematara a puerta, aunque el guardameta mexicano tapó bien el disparo. La Rojita jugaba de memoria, con la desenvoltura de quien se sabe superior. Como manda el guion de los amistosos, Gallardo revolucionó el once al descanso, introduciendo savia nueva en cada línea. No se amilanó España pese a los cambios, aunque su fútbol perdió algo de la mordiente y la llegada que había exhibido en la primera mitad. El partido, más trabado, pedía un golpe de calidad para sentenciarse. Y ese golpe llegó de la mano de los frescos. Corralejo puso a correr al espacio a Morante, y este, con apenas un par de toques, soltó un latigazo con la zurda imposible para el meta mexicano que cerró definitivamente la contienda. El 2-0 rubricó una noche redonda para una generación que sigue engordando su leyenda y que dedicó el triunfo, allá donde estuviera, a Ceuta.

articles.title: Meet the only Scot managing an international team
articles.summary: More than 4,000 miles from his native Dundee, Kurt Herd is flying the flag for Scotland in international football - as manager of Dominica's national side.
articles.body:
More than 4,000 miles from his native Dundee, Kurt Herd is flying the flag for Scotland in international football.

The 34-year old is manager of Dominica, the Carribbean island, making him the only Scottish manager currently leading an international men's side.

"I'll be calling my mum and dad with that one," Herd laughs.

Appointed permanently in August after a short-term stint, Herd's role is not exactly like the one held by Steve Clarke, or his successor, Sebastien Pocognoli, though.

Herd is not just Dominica's manager but effectively their analyst, scout, nutritionist, and yoga instructor rolled into one, given he is the only full-time staff member for the team. Including the players.

"A real whirlwind the last few weeks, but it's been amazing for me as a coach to go and test myself," Herd tells BBC Scotland.

"It's been the toughest but the greatest three or four weeks of my career so far."

At 34, Herd has already packed a lot in. The former Dundee United academy coach has worked in Sweden, Australia, Malaysia and Kyrgysztan.

He has met Arsene Wenger and other big football figures along the way and now his task is to improve the world's 182nd-best side, made up of largely amateur players from an island population of about 65,000.

Will Pocognoli change goalkeeper after Swiss loss?

New coach, new players, but same old failings hamper Scotland

Hampden debut to forget, but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture

Scrolling for players & setting the tone

Most of Dominica's players play in their own domestic league, which Herd roughly equates to League 2 in Scotland.

While other Carribbean nations like Haiti and Curacao have made use of a lot overseas players to help them reach the World Cup, rules in Dominica limit them to having six.

A rule change in January will allow Herd to start at least start recruiting players with Dominican grandparents.

Former St Mirren and Livingston goalkeeper Shamal George, now at Bromley, is one Herd has been able to identify through social media and the use of talent-spotters.

"I sit on Instagram for two or three hours and I'm just looking at player profiles, trying to see if somebody's got a little Dominica flag in that bio page," Herd says.

"I'm on the phone constantly. Whether that's scrolling social media - and it's not for fun - it's because I'm looking at players' profiles and databases.

"I've got people that are doing that for me as well. I've got people in the US, Canada, Europe, UK, that their job for me is to contact clubs, contact agents, contact players, come back to me and tell me, yeah, coach, we've got one. And those guys have been absolutely priceless to me."

Recruitment is not the only tool Herd is deploying to try to raise the standards as Dominica compete in the Concacaf Nations League B this autumn.

The squad are now performing yoga and other mindfulness techniques, while Herd is always re-enforcing dietary and sleep advice to the group to go with his team and one-to-one coaching.

He even makes sure he is up running every morning and is never seen with a beer at night so he can try to set professional standards in view of his adopted community.

"It's tough, to be honest - it's relentless," he admits. "I'm doing everything at the minute.

"I'm the full-time member of staff, so it all falls on my shoulders. Everybody else has got jobs. I've got one assistant coach that I work with, but he's a school teacher.

"Even now we're in camp, he's still working. He's still trying to teach kids. I don't mind it because I feel like I need to control the situation for now because we're in a cycle of change.

"And it has to be me that drives that change. And I have to show people why we're doing it and how we're doing it."

Herd has been in Dominica for two years now, having worked with the youth sides before in his role as a talent coach with Fifa.

He says he has "fallen in love" with the country and its people, who consider him one of them now.

Life on a beautiful Carribbean island is good, but Herd admits being "obsessed" with football means he cannot always fully enjoy the trappings that come with it.

That drive has been with him throughout his career, from when he left Scotland for Australia without a job after graduating from Abertay University and ended up coaching a team, Magic FC.

The journey has taken him to the bustling metropolis of Kuala Lumpur, where he worked with Spanish club Villareal's Asian arm, to the high mountains of Kyrgysztan, where goats blocking the road once held up a training session for four hours.

At times, it has been tough. Missing family events and milestones has not been easy. However, the experience of working across so many football cultures has been rewarding, as have some of the other moments along the way.

That includes playing five-a-side against former Portugal striker Nuno Gomes at a Fifa event in Paraguay and - nearly - Arsene Wenger in Zurich.

"We get given the teams before and I'm like, 'oh my God, I'm on Arsene Wenger's team.' I've taken a photo of that, I've sent it back home. Unbelievable.

"So we've got ready, gone on the field and we're warming up and a little bit of drizzle comes through.

"And I'm looking for Arsene. I'm going, where's Arsene gone? So we've gone down into the restaurant and Arsene's just sitting there with a bottle of red wine.

"He's like, 'no man, the rain, it's not for me. When I was in London, I have enough'. So we're soaked through. He's sitting there with a nice red wine, enjoying himself."

Herd's not sure where his coaching journey will take him next, but his ambition is to eventually get into the club game at as high a level as possible.

The Dundonian has already shown his willingness to adapt and learn - and take on big challenges.

"I want this on a daily basis," he says. "I want that pressure. I want that day-to-day grind."

For now, it's back to wearing his many hats with Dominica in their quest for Nations League promotion.

articles.title: Feroz ataque a Guardiola: "O Pep lo sabía y es un fraude o estaba ciego"
articles.standfirst: Matthew Syed atiza en The Times al entrenador español tras el veredicto del caso City
articles.summary: Matthew Syed atiza en The Times al entrenador español tras el veredicto del caso City
articles.body: En Inglaterra, el caso del Manchester City y las irregularidades financieras de las que ha sido declarado culpable, están empezando a salpicar también a Pep Guardiola. En un duro artículo en el diario 'The Times', uno de los más prestigiosos del país, el columnista Matthew Syed habla de legado "manchado" del técnico español y se cuestiona si es un fraude, por estar al tanto de las irregularidades", o miope por no darse cuenta de ellas. La investigación de la Premier League que ha desembocado en esta culpabilidad se alarga entre 2009 y 2018 y cubre dos de las temporadas en las que estuvo Guardiola en el club inglés, incluyendo en la que conquistó su primera liga inglesa. "Ahora sabemos que dirigió a un club adulterado, pagado por contratos adulterados, alimentado por compañías adulteradas y durante la que ahora podemos denominar con una era adulterada", comienza este duro artículo contra el City y el técnico de Sampedor. "Hay dos alternativas", se cuestiona el columnista tras mencionar los más de 1.000 millones de euros que defraudó el City en esos casi diez años. "O Pep lo sabía y por lo tanto no es ni un visionario ni una leyenda, solo un fraude, o no lo sabía y entonces es la persona más miope. Me refiero, yo no soy un contable forense, pero he cuestionado durante más de una década los arreglos financieros del City, pese a recibir constantes insultos y amenazas. ¿Y Pep no vio nada? ¿Está ciego?". "Por supuesto hay una tercera alternativa, la hipocresía", sentencia el periodista. Este miércoles, Guardiola publicó el primer comunicado tras anunciarse la culpabilidad del City, expresando su apoyo al club inglés en el que pasó nueve temporadas, ganando todos los títulos posibles, incluyendo seis Premier League y una Liga de Campeones. "Quiero que cada aficionado del Manchester City sepa que estoy aquí; más que nunca. Siempre he estado, estoy y siempre estaré, detrás de mi club, mi dueño, mi presidente, Ferran, los jugadores, el personal, Enzo y vosotros, nuestros extraordinarios aficionados. Dejadme ser claro: superaremos esto juntos. Os quiero a todos", aseguró Guardiola. "Guardiola es de forma incuestionable un gran estrategia que ha sido exitoso en muchos clubes, pero seamos honestos, su legado siempre estará enmarcado en un periodo en el Etihad en el que la verdadera magia la hacían los contables, no un entrenador", finalizó el artículo.

articles.title: Final farewell? Ronaldo abruptly leaves Portugal camp, promises truth 'in due time' and wishes team-mates 'good luck'
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's sudden departure from the Portugal national team camp raises questions about his future in international football. After a clash with coach Jorge Jesus, Ronaldo promises to reveal the truth later, leaving fans and teammates in suspense.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has abruptly left Portugal’s national team camp one day before the UEFA Nations League meeting with Denmark, after a turbulent few days involving his role under new head coach Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old confirmed his departure in a statement on Wednesday, saying he would reveal the reasons “in due time” while wishing Portugal and his team-mates good luck. Whether the decision marks a farewell to international football remains to be seen.Ronaldo confirms he has left Portugal campRonaldo confirmed his departure from the Portugal camp on Wednesday, September 30, in a statement posted on his official social media accounts. The announcement came as Jesus held a press conference ahead of Portugal’s match against Denmark in Copenhagen. The Portugal captain said his decision followed the coach’s comments and a conversation with Proença, who had changed his schedule to travel to Copenhagen as tensions over Ronaldo’s role in the team grew.“After the National Team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the National Team training camp,” Ronaldo wrote.He then indicated that he would explain what had happened at a later stage.“In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.”Ronaldo finished by wishing Portugal and his team-mates well.“Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”The Portuguese Football Federation confirmed that Ronaldo had left the camp, while saying the remaining squad would continue preparing for the Denmark match and the subsequent Nations League fixture against Norway.Ronaldo was seen leaving Parken Stadium in a Portuguese Football Federation vehicle as his team-mates arrived for training, according to Portuguese newspaper A Bola. His private jet was also reported to have been preparing to take him away from Denmark. Reuters later reported that the aircraft had left Madrid for Copenhagen and was scheduled to return to the Spanish capital.Ronaldo remians Portugal's most-capped player and leading scorer, with 234 appearances and 146 goals for his country.Jorge Jesus had told Ronaldo he would not start against DenmarkThe dispute developed after Ronaldo was left on the bench for Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway.Jesus selected João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos in attack, with Ramos scoring Portugal's winning goal after Erling Haaland had equalised. Ronaldo warmed up during the second half but was not introduced.Jesus had previously said he wanted to manage Ronaldo's workload after the forward played almost 70 minutes against Wales in Portugal's opening Nations League match.Ronaldo then went directly to the dressing room after the Norway victory rather than joining his teammates in celebrating with the travelling supporters.The situation continued into Portugal's preparations for Denmark.Jesus said on Wednesday that Ronaldo would train with the team, while also confirming that he would not start against Denmark.“Yesterday, he did not refuse to train,” Jesus said.“Francisco Conceicao did not train because he was injured, and Joao Felix because we tried to ease his fatigue, while Cristiano did work in the gym. Today he will train. It is the fourth day, so he will train.”Jesus then explained the decision he had made over Ronaldo's role.“I can promise what I want. I am the coach. I told the player that he would not start the match, and that he would be on the substitutes' bench.”“If I need him for 30 minutes then he will play, and if I do not need him then he will not play.”Jesus also made clear that nobody would influence his selection.“No player will change my mind, neither him nor anyone else in football, not even any president, that will never happen.”Ronaldo left the camp after the press conference.Pedro Proença travelled to address the situationThe Portuguese Football Federation president changed his schedule and travelled to Copenhagen as the situation around Ronaldo and Jesus escalated.Proença held talks with the parties involved on Wednesday morning after the disagreement that followed Ronaldo's omission against Norway.Jesus had maintained that there was no major problem between himself and Ronaldo and said his conversations with the captain had been normal.Ronaldo, however, had missed three consecutive training sessions according to A Bola, despite Jesus saying shortly before his departure that he expected the forward to train.The Portuguese newspaper reported that Ronaldo left the Parken Stadium in a Portuguese Football Federation vehicle as his teammates arrived for training.His departure came only minutes after Jesus' press conference.Earlier reports had said Ronaldo was unhappy with the decision to leave him out against Norway and with the uncertainty surrounding his starting place against Denmark.Ronaldo's retirement remains unconfirmedPortugal now face Denmark on Thursday without Ronaldo in the squad, with the team leading Nations League Group A4 after two victories.Portugal have six points, three clear of both Denmark and Norway.Ronaldo's departure does not amount to an official retirement announcement. He has not said that he is ending his international career, while the Portuguese Football Federation has not announced his retirement.His final words before leaving camp, however, have prompted immediate questions because he said he would reveal the reasons for his decision later and then wished Portugal and all his teammates good luck.Ronaldo has spent more than two decades representing Portugal, becoming the country's record appearance holder and scorer while winning the 2016 European Championship and the 2019 Nations League. articles.title: La aerolínea Etihad sopesa medidas legales contra la Premier por el caso del City
articles.standfirst: Rechaza categóricamente estar involucrada en "acuerdos comerciales impropios"
articles.summary: Rechaza categóricamente estar involucrada en "acuerdos comerciales impropios"
articles.body: La aerolínea de Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Etihad, uno de los principales patrocinadores del Manchester City, ha negado los cargos de los que se ha culpado al club inglés y sopesa tomar medidas legales contra la Premier League. Etihad es una de las empresa involucradas en la adulteración de las cuentas financieras que llevó a cabo el City durante nueve años y que sirvió para inflar sus ingresos de forma irreal y lograr un beneficio ilegal de más de 1000 millones de euros durante dicho periodo. En un comunicado, la aerolínea "categóricamente rechaza cualquier investigación, conclusión o implicación que sugiera que esta empresa ha estado involucrada en acuerdos comerciales impropios". Según Etihad, la Premier League en ningún momento se puso en contacto con ellos y no les dio la oportunidad de proveer información relevante. Ahora Etihad está buscando consejo legal para llevar acciones contra la Premier y proteger sus intereses. Etihad, que es una empresa valorada en cerca de 5.000 millones de euros, ha sido el principal patrocinador del City, dando nombre a su estadio, desde 2009. En todo este tiempo ha inyectado cientos de millones en las arcas del club. "La comunicación pública de la Premier League sobre la investigación de la comisión, después de un periodo de filtraciones selectivas, ha creado daños a Etihad, pese a que la aerolínea no ha sido mencionada en dicho informa. Etihad está muy preocupada por cómo este asunto ha sido comunicado públicamente. La falta de claridad y transparencia, además de la selecta 'desvelación' de información, ha supuesto daños para Etihad. La Premier League debe asumir las consecuencias de cómo esta investigación ha sido presentada". "Etihad está inmensamente orgullosa de su larga relación con el Manchester City. El nombre de Etihad ha sido llevado con orgullo por el club y su estadio durante muchos años y como parte de esta relación hemos conectado a millones de aficionados alrededor del mundo. Nuestro compromiso con el Manchester City, sus aficionados y nuestros acuerdos continúa siendo fuerte", informó la compañía.

articles.title: Lyon 0-0 Chelsea: Lauren James sees penalty overturned by VAR as Blues draw with eight-time Women's Champions League winners
articles.summary: Report as Chelsea draw at last season's beaten Women's Champions League finalists Lyon; Lauren James wastes best chance and sees penalty overturned by VAR, while Ada Hegerberg is denied by superb Hannah Hampton save
articles.body:
James initially appeared to have been brought down by Damaris Egurrola inside the Lyon box with only minutes remaining, but having initially given the penalty, referee Marta Huerta de Aza overturned her decision after consulting the VAR review monitor.

Both sides could have won the game at the Parc Olympique Lyonnais, with Ada Hegerberg forcing Hannah Hampton into a superb full-length save in added time.

Until that point, both sides had struggled to create clear-cut chances in the south of France, with substitute James arguably the most guilty of wasting one of few significant opportunities when she fired straight at Maria Grohs from Alyssa Thompson's pull back.

Beyond that, there was little to separate the sides who both appeared content to settle for a draw in Sonia Bompastor's first return to her former side, who she won the Champions League with in 2022.

Bompastor: We created enough to win the game

Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor on Paramount Plus:

"Coming into the game, we knew the tactics would be important both on and off the ball. We had a plan and I'm really happy with our performance on the ball. We exploited many positions on the pitch and behind the back line.

"We created enough to win the game, so we're a bit disappointed. With the quality of Lauren James, her chance should have gone in but it happens. It's early in the season.

"Playing against Sunday on Arsenal was a good thing, but we couldn't prepare for this the way we wanted to with fresh legs and tactically.

"The team is together, right now, which is really important. The players understand what we want to do."

Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze to Disney+:

"We dominated possession, but it's a fair result. They had some good counter-attacking moments, they were on top at the end but that's what happens when two top teams play against each other.

"A draw for both teams, at this time of the season, is probably not the worst thing.

"We worked our socks off and I'm just proud of every single player, especially considering we played a very difficult game three days ago [against Arsenal]."

articles.body: Buenas noticias para Rubén Albés. Ismaël Gharbi podrá regresar antes de lo previsto a Leganés después de que la selección de Túnez haya dado por terminada su concentración y cancelado el amistoso que tenía previsto disputar este sábado ante Mali. La finalización anticipada de la concentración abre definitivamente la puerta a su regreso. Rubén Albés recupera así una pieza importante después de no poder contar con el internacional tunecino frente al Castellón. articles.title: Una carrera al aeropuerto para intentar convencer a Cristiano y una sensación: su retirada es definitiva
articles.standfirst: Jorge Jesus y Pedro Proença hicieron una intentona de última hora para frenar a Ronaldo
articles.summary: Jorge Jesus y Pedro Proença hicieron una intentona de última hora para frenar a Ronaldo
articles.body: El terremoto Cristiano sigue teniendo réplicas. Su sorpresiva marcha, a media tarde del miércoles, de la concentración de Portugal tras escuchar a su seleccionador decir en rueda de prensa, que "en este equipo, yo estoy al mando" y desvelar su plan de suplencias para el mito luso sigue haciendo ruido y dejando detalles sorprendentes. En Portugal se da por hecho que esta marcha significa una retirada definitiva de Cristiano Ronaldo de la selección nacional. Fueron 23 años de Cristiano con la camiseta lusa, puso el nombre de Portugal en todos los rincones del mundo, le dio tres títulos a su país (Una Eurocopa y dos Nations Leagues) y este cierre triste y abrupto empaña de alguna forma su historia global con el equipo nacional. Nadie esperaba que una historia de tanto éxito pudiese tener un final así. Lo que debería terminar con una fiesta tremenda en un partido de la selección portuguesa y con un gran homenaje acaba de esta manera fría y extraña cuyos detalles se siguen conociendo poco a poco. Cristiano Ronaldo, que llegaba a Dinamarca con el resto del equipo, decidió después de escuchar las palabras de su seleccionador abandonar el estadio donde se preparaba para entrenar. Se fue al hotel, cogió la maleta y pidió que su avión privado, que estaba en Madrid, pusiera rumbo a Copenhague para recogerle. El avión aterrizó en la capital danesa sobre las 22.15 de la noche (hora peninsular española) y volvió a despegar hacia Madrid a las 23.35 horas. Con Cristiano en el aparato, dejando atrás a sus compañeros, se ponía fin a la etapa de Ronaldo en la selección de Portugal. En tierra quedaban también dos protagonistas de la historia, que hicieron una última intentona de convencer al futbolista. Jorge Jesus, seleccionador, y Pedro Proença, presidente de la federación, se fueron tras Cristiano al aeropuerto para intentar retenerle en Copenhague, junto al resto de los jugadores convocados. Pero pese a sus intentos, el gran capitán de Portugal no atendió a razones, se montó en el avión y les dejó plantados.

articles.title: New Rumors on College Football Playoff Expansion Update Buzz on 24-Team Bracket, Schedule Format
articles.summary: A 24-team College Football Playoff reportedly "feels like a foregone conclusion."
articles.body:
A 24-team College Football Playoff reportedly "feels like a foregone conclusion."

Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports reported as much Wednesday, noting CFP executives held their first in-person meeting during a 30-day negotiating window with ESPN regarding the future of the postseason format.

Those meetings, which included conference commissioners, featured discussions about schedules and eliminating conference championship games. The deadline for CFP leaders and ESPN to come to terms on a new format is Oct. 9, otherwise the 24-team idea would go to the open market ahead of the Dec. 1 deadline for deciding whether there will be an expanded field for the 2027 season.

"We've worked through a lot of the other issues associated with [a 24-team] expansion and those things needed to happen before we started any kind of negotiation [over money]," CFP executive director Rich Clark said.

As Dellenger noted, the 24-team field started as a proposal from the Big Ten last August and now counts the ACC, Big 12 and Notre Dame as proponents.

While the SEC initially showed "staunch opposition," commissioner Greg Sankey showed "a sign of openness" last month when he circulated requirements for such a field that included all power conference teams to play at least 10 games against power conference opponents.

Clark even provided early hints at what the schedule would look like with the eight first-round games "ideally" slated for the week after the regular season when conference championship games typically take place.

The eight second-round games would also "most likely" be on campus in the third week of December.

There are still things to sort out, such as what to do with the Army-Navy game in December and other bowls, but it seems like progress is being made toward a 24-team field even if it means sacrificing the approximately $250 million generated by conference championship games.

"The money is there," one CFP stakeholder told Dellenger, although Clark said, "The revenue is an unknown. That's why we're in this negotiating window."

Dellenger's report suggests the conference in-fighting may be coming to an end as the sport moves toward the 24-team CFP format.

For now, though, there is still a 12-team format in place for the current season with first-round games played on the campus of the better seed. But there could be twice as many teams vying for spots as soon as next season.

articles.title: 'If we can get a decent deal, we are definitely going to 24' — CFP leaders discussing logistics of 24-team playoff
articles.summary: CFP leaders are closer than ever to expanding to a 24-team playoff. They are talking buyouts of conference title games and more in preparation.
articles.body:
ROSEMONT, Ill. — College Football Playoff leaders on Wednesday took another step down what's been a long, winding road to expanding the sport's postseason to 24 teams.

The fact that it happened here, in a Chicago suburb, within the headquarters of the Big Ten, came only as a coincidence. The league that originally pitched the 24-team playoff model hosted the annual gathering.

The consensus: A doubling of the postseason feels like a foregone conclusion — even if no one will say it publicly.

"We've worked through a lot of the other issues associated with [a 24-team] expansion and those things needed to happen before we started any kind of negotiation [over money]," CFP executive director Rich Clark said, peeling back the curtain a bit.

Discussions over a 24-team playoff field, introduced as a realistic proposal by the Big Ten last August, have accelerated this summer and, now, into the fall: From the SEC's staunch opposition to the format last fall, to the Big Ten blocking an expansion to 16 teams in January; from the ACC, Big 12 and Notre Dame shifting positions from 16 to 24 teams in March, to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey last month circulating requirements related to expansion — a sign of openness to accept a 24-team field (he's requiring all power league teams to play 10 games against power conference programs).

Here in Chicago, CFP executives held their first in-person gathering since deciding to enter into the 30-day negotiating window with ESPN over an expanded field (the most-discussed model is 23 at-large selections plus a spot for the highest-ranked Group of Six program).

Conference commissioners are talking schedules, logistics and the elimination of their league championship games — all conversations held with ESPN as the network works to deliver a formal offer ahead of the expiration of its negotiating window (Oct. 9).

Things are serious — enough that Clark, when asked, revealed some of the schedule of a 24-team field. The new eight first-round games would "ideally" start a week after the regular season ends, he said, leaving an open week where the conference championship games are currently played. Also, the eight second-round games will "most likely" be played on the campus of the better seed in the third week of December, he said.

Would CFP executives really spend hundreds of hours of time over scheduling and logistics only to decide against expanding to 24 teams? It's unlikely, especially when considering that "the money is there," as one CFP stakeholder told Yahoo Sports. It's a reference to the single biggest determining factor on expansion: Can the power leagues recuperate the revenue lost from the elimination of their conference championship games?

That figure is believed to be at least $250 million.

"The revenue is an unknown," Clark said Wednesday. "That's why we're in this negotiating window."

CFP leaders and ESPN executives have until Oct. 9 to come to terms before CFP officials take their 24-team product to the open market. If that transpires, they'll have about two months until another deadline of Dec. 1 — a date in which expansion must be determined for a new playoff in 2027.

In the meantime, scheduling logistics remain one of the highest hurdles, specifically the situation with the Army-Navy game, one of the most-watched affairs traditionally played on the second Saturday in December. In a 24-team model, the game may move up a week, to the first Saturday in December, where conference championships now reside.

The game would kick off six days after the CFP committee selects the field. What if Army or Navy is in contention for a playoff spot?

What happens to the bowl games? While six bowls are incorporated into the CFP rotation, roughly a dozen other games that traditionally host power league teams will see their participants slip out of the top 25.

As reported at Yahoo Sports this spring , conference executives have been discussing the creation of a 10-bowl lineup that pits power conference programs against one another in a deal where the media rights would be controlled by the leagues and not the bowls.

Meanwhile, as Army-Navy and the bowls get sorted out, the road to a 24-team playoff is growing more and more clear.

"If we can get a decent [TV] deal, we are definitely going to 24," said one confident stakeholder.

articles.title: Panthers to break decade-long drought on Sunday Night Football
articles.summary: No matter the outcome on Sunday night, the Panthers will break a decade-long drought when they host the Lions here in Week 4.
articles.body:
This week, the Carolina Panthers will get a rare moment under the lights—as they host the Detroit Lions in a prime-time matchup on Sunday night. And if it feels like a long time since the Panthers have been featured on Sunday Night Football , that's because it has been.

The last Sunday nighter for Carolina was nearly 10 years ago, on Dec. 4, 2016—when they got blown out by the Seattle Seahawks , 40-7.

This was a pretty infamous game, beginning with former head coach Ron Rivera (and/or former general manager Dave Gettleman) benching quarterback and reigning Most Valuable Player Cam Newton on the first play for not wearing a tie to the stadium. Backup Derek Anderson , in his stead, tossed a pick-six on his very first pass.

A lot of pressure comes with these games, and the competition in this case won't help. Carolina will host a Detroit team that's won 36 games over the last three seasons. Plus, they'll be vulnerable where the Lions are best—as their potent passing game will surely attack the absences of cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson .

Rivales: "Me gusta mucho Raphinha, es muy importante para su equipo, mete muchos goles, quizá no tiene el reconocimiento que merece. articles.standfirst: Gran gol del canario Nico Paz, al más puro estilo de Leo Messi, en el triunfo de Argentina por 4-0 contra Bolivia
articles.summary: Gran gol del canario Nico Paz, al más puro estilo de Leo Messi, en el triunfo de Argentina por 4-0 contra Bolivia
articles.body: La Selección Argentina goleó por 4-0 a la de Bolivia en un partido amistoso jugado en el Estadio Mario Kempes, el primero desde la final del Mundial 2026 que perdió contra España y a 6 días del encuentro contra Benín que marcará la despedida de Lionel Messi de la Albiceleste. Lautaro Martínez en el minuto 19, Nico Paz en el 29, Cristian 'Cuti' Romero (m.52) y José Manuel 'Flaco' López (m.86), marcaron los goles de la selección dirigida por Lionel Scaloni. Martínez y Romero, dos de los anotadores, han sido los capitanes elegidos por Scaloni en ausencia de Messi. Con aforo reducido para cumplir con la sanción impuesta por la FIFA, el partido marcó el debut de Román Vega, Ezequiel Fernández, Santiago Simón, Leonel Flores y Valentín Gómez. De esta forma, el seleccionador completó hoy 70 jugadores promovidos al estrenos con el equipo absoluto. Para Bolivia, en tanto, es la segunda derrota tras quedar eliminada en la repesca al Mundial con Irak. El domingo pasado había perdido por 2-0 ante Paraguay en el Audi Field de Washington. El partido exhibió un amplio dominio del equipo local, que rompió el equilibrio en el minuto 19 tras un pase en profundidad de Alexis Mac Allister para la definición de Lautaro Martínez ante Guillermo Viscarra. El segundo tanto llegó en el minuto 29 con un pase de Exequiel Palacios. A continuación 'Nico' Paz la picó ante la salida de Viscarra. Luego Argentina dosificó el esfuerzo. Llegó entonces una rotación de jugadores en el comienzo del segundo tiempo y en el minuto 52 'Cuti' Romero amplió. El último gol llegó a dos minutos del final con un arranque de Leonel Flores y una asistencia a 'el Flaco' López, quien firmó su primer gol con la Albiceleste. Luego de esta goleada, Argentina afrontará dos duelos en el Estadio Monumental de Núñez, el sábado contra Burkina Faso y el martes contra Benín, el rival que observará de primera mano la despedida de la selección de Lionel Messi. 4.⁠ ⁠Argentina: Emiliano Martínez; Agustín Giay (m.73, Santiago Simón), Cristian Romero (m.55, Leonardo Balerdi), Lisandro Martínez (m.80, Valentín Gómez), Román Vega; Gianluca Prestianni (m.55, Valentín Barco), Alexis Mac Allister (m.73, Ezequiel Fernández), Exequiel Palacios (m.80, Leonel Flores), Nico Paz (m.55, Franco Mastantuono); Julián Álvarez y Lautaro Martínez (m.73, Juan Manuel López). articles.summary: El central y capitán se ha destapado como el gran goleador del equipo caballa, que empieza a ver la luz tras un horroroso inicio de Liga
articles.body: En su tercera temporada en el Ceuta, Carlos Hernández se ha convertido en el imprevisto referente ofensivo del equipo. El veterano central jiennense suma cuatro tantos en siete jornadas tras encadenar tres partidos viendo puerta. Después de rescatar el primer punto de la temporada con un gol al Valladolid en el minuto 101, el zaguero certificó la pasada jornada la primera victoria del curso al firmar un brillante doblete ante la Real Sociedad B. Tres puntos de oro que suponen un balón de oxígeno deportivo y un motivo de celebración en medio de la crisis migratoria que vive la ciudad. El pilar de la defensa caballa no oculta el alivio que ha supuesto para el vestuario inaugurar por fin el casillero de triunfos: "Llevamos una racha mala. No hemos empezado de la mejor forma, así que esto es una alegría para todos nosotros. Un rayo de luz en la situación en la que estamos; a ver si podemos arrancar". En este sentido, Hernández recalca la importancia de ir recuperando efectivos tras un inicio accidentado por los problemas físicos, señalando que han "tenido muchas bajas a inicio de temporada y de jugadores importantes. Koné vuelve y da asistencias, Anuar hizo un buen partido; los necesitamos a todos". A pesar de liderar la tabla de goleadores de la plantilla y ser segundo en el Pichichi, el propio jugador reconoce cierta incredulidad ante su racha realizadora: "Estoy sorprendido porque normalmente algún gol cae, pero no pensaba que iba a marcar tres semanas seguidas y doblete. Pero yo prefiero ganar y no meter ningún gol, aunque anímicamente sí es verdad que el tanto del empate del otro día ayudó mucho en la confianza del equipo para culminar esta semana con la victoria". Una faceta rematadora que guarda relación con sus inicios en el fútbol base: "Empecé como pivote defensivo, pero un entrenador me dijo que si quería llegar a algo, sería como central, y jugué desde Juveniles. Es verdad que de cabeza me desenvuelvo bien: metí seis un año y al siguiente, cuatro con el Oviedo, pero el año pasado tuve muchas ocasiones y marqué menos. Sinceramente, no quiero que me venga la ansiedad de delantero, porque mi trabajo es otro", ha reconocido. Consciente de lo inusual que resulta ver a un central en lo alto de la tabla de realizadores, el andaluz admite entre sonrisas su idilio con el gol. "Nos está costando marcar desde la primera jornada. En Segunda división hay que aprovechar las ocasiones, y ahora estoy con la flor", comenta el futbolista, sin perder el foco de su cometido principal en el verde: "Firmo no marcar ningún gol más y conseguir la permanencia. Lo de los goles es secundario, sobre todo en esta categoría, que lo más importante es no encajar. Yo me castigo en pensar que no hay que encajar tanto, es mi primer objetivo", ha insistido. Por último, en su tercer año plenamente integrado en el club y en el entorno caballa, el central no permanece ajeno al impacto que este triunfo tiene en la calle dada la coyuntura social. "A los jugadores, el día a día no nos afecta en nada. Hacemos vida normal, pero soy padre y entiendo a la gente que lo puede estar pasando mal por la ciudad. Me quedo con que esta victoria haya sido una alegría para los ceutíes, una esperanza a la que agarrarse. Tenemos que seguir y no rendirnos, ni nosotros como equipo ni ellos", concluyó.

articles.summary: Los armeros han sumado 64 puntos en las 30 jornadas disputadas en 2026 y su ritmo de puntuación es más alto incluso que el del primer año en Segunda
articles.body: El Eibar despidió 2025 con la preocupación en el cuerpo después de un final de año complicado en el que llegó a tocar los puestos de descenso. Sin embargo, 2026 ha cambiado por completo el rumbo de un equipo que estuvo a punto de rozar el milagro de meterse en los playoffs hace cuatro meses y que ha comenzado la presente campaña como un tiro para firmar un récord nunca visto en Ipurua en el fútbol profesional: seis triunfos consecutivos. La cautela permanece de puertas hacia dentro. Y es que en el club armero saben mejor que nadie que esto sólo es el comienzo y no conviene lanzar las campanas al vuelo. Pero lo que realmente invita al optimismo es que la sobresaliente trayectoria de este arranque de competición es la continuación de la histórica segunda vuelta que firmó la pasada campaña con 46 puntos. La continuidad del bloque y la apuesta por Jokin Aranbarri han permitido mantener el listón con el que concluyó el curso anterior. De hecho, el Eibar es el equipo que más puntos ha sumado en Segunda en 2026. El cuadro azulgrana ha logrado 64 puntos en los 30 partidos que se han disputado este año, una cifra estratosférica que nadie más iguala. El Castellón sigue la estela del cuadro armero con 60 puntos, mientras que el Almería y el Burgos suman 57. En total, el Eibar ha logrado 20 victorias, 4 empates y 6 derrotas en los últimos nueve meses de competición. Casi nada. Los armeros promedian más de dos puntos por partido, han logrado 46 goles y sólo han encajado 22. Todavía quedan 12 partidos por disputarse en lo que queda de 2026 y, aunque mantener este ritmo será bastante complicado, la realidad es que tiene al alcance de su mano batir todos los registros de puntos sumados en año natural. Su mejor año, hasta ahora, fue 2022, donde logró la friolera de 75 puntos con Gaizka Garitano en el banquillo, mientras que en 2023 llegó a los 66, cifra que superará ganando un partido. El ritmo de este Eibar es similar a aquel equipo que sumó 80 puntos en el primer año en Segunda y aun así no le dio para volver a Primera. Los armeros se irían hasta los 89 puntos en el caso de mantener esta trayectoria, algo impensable a finales de 2025, cuando el equipo coqueteaba peligrosamente con los puestos de descenso.
